correctness.rationale: The bigram Euler-trail uniqueness argument is direct. In the inspected 2016 Proposition 5.7 finite decomposition, at most q disjoint nonempty cyclic letter-root supports occur; equality s=q forces one-letter roots exhausting the alphabet. Corollary 5.5 excludes all external occurrences, hence all connectors. Lemma 5.10 gives finitely many types with at most s-1 length degrees of freedom, so nonchain singleton words are O_q(n^(q-2)). Verified the finite checker on exact package code; no infinite inference from enumeration.

Neither cited source states that implication as an all-q enumeration theorem. Their hypotheses suffice with the additional argument given.

originality.rationale: The first 2016 source proves only big-O and formulates general sharpness as a conjecture; the second 2016 source gives exact binary and ternary examples but not the q>=4 leading constant or typical form. The new coefficient for every q>=4 is not the earlier big-O bound and is not obtained just by restating small cases. Residual risk of an independent unindexed derivation remains.
residual_risks: This sharp coefficient may have been derived but not indexed in independent later work.

value.rationale: The problem is explicitly tied to the published conjecture that the singleton exponent is attained. For all fixed alphabets q>=4, the result supplies not only the exponent but the sharp coefficient q and asymptotic classification of typical singletons, offering a motivated infinite family not resolved by the earlier q2/q3 formulas. It does not overstate higher-factor-length cases.
